visualReview.notes: All 12 current portable frames inspected: preview, four turntables, two whole-tower sides, restaurant/platform close view, lattice mast detail, square base, roof plan and distant silhouette. Narrow cast-concrete shaft, five service platforms, dish rims/feed supports, twelve-faceted flared pod, stepped roof and continuous tapering mast render intact. Named detail cameras intentionally crop neighboring levels; complete-tower views include the 124 m tip and ground.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: All 12 current sky-PMREM shared frames inspected, including the north-up placement. Shared concrete and painted metal preserve metric surface detail, white glazing frames and open lattice bracing; the unique dark glass fallback remains correctly bound. Geographic loading, shared material reuse and distant unloading passed. The square hipped base follows the source-local footprint and the circular upper structure stays centered.

geographicReview.notes: Co-centered exact Q1935277 map parts locate the tower; way474904229 provides the square ground base and horizontal axes. The mapped small/large circular-part labels are visibly reversed relative to owner photographs, so the raw labels are preserved but the 7.2 m shaft and 17.4 m pod are reconstructed from actual photographic/geometry evidence. North-up placement confirms the square outline. The rotational shaft/pod require no invented front; antenna phases remain representative. The separately mapped adjoining office wings are excluded.

fidelityReview.notes: Passed for the detailed permanent exterior reconstruction at the requested world-viewer scope. Owner height, opening year and current aerial/close photographs establish the 124 m silhouette, five platforms, flared glazing, white roof, square base and lattice antenna. Historical society gives 7.2 m shaft diameter, while the map supplies the 17.4 m projected pod and base shape. Intermediate platform and roof levels, truss sizes, glazing subdivisions and telecommunications fittings are proportional reconstruction. The source explicitly preserves conflicting map-part classifications and approximate 74/75 m restaurant-floor descriptions. Changing equipment, projection lighting, the rotating interior and separately mapped offices are outside this asset scope.
